intro_md:
**Week 1 · Lesson 5 – Getting around (~40 min).** On Saturday Nam needs a SIM card. Learn the words for finding your way, see them on a map, then listen.

| Part | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| ① Learn | Directions & transport: *opposite, next to, get on/off, take the tram* – with a map | 8 min |
| ② Try it | 6 quick checks on the map | 5 min |
| ③ Listen | Jess gives directions (3 rounds) | 12 min |
| ④ Listen | The fifteen-minute city (3 rounds) | 12 min |
| ✓ | Feedback + 📤 Submit | 2 min |

parts.title: Finding your way – words on a map
parts.md:
![Map of Hope Street](data/img/w1/l5-map.svg)

**Place words** – look at the map while you read:

| Chunk | Meaning | On the map |
|---|---|---|
| **opposite** | on the other side of the street, facing | The tram stop is **opposite** the church. |
| **next to** | right beside | The phone shop is **next to** the bank. |
| **at the end of the street** | where the street stops | The church is **at the end of** Hope Street. |
| **on the corner** | where two streets meet | The café is **on the corner**. |
| **turn left / right** | change direction | Go out of the café and **turn left**. |
| **go past** | walk by something without stopping | **Go past** the park. |

**Transport chunks:**

| Chunk | Example |
|---|---|
| **take the tram / bus** | *Take the tram* to Market Street. |
| **get on ↔ get off** | *Get on* at Hope Street, *get off* at Market Street. 🇻🇳 lên xe ↔ xuống xe |
| **it's (three stops / a ten-minute walk)** | *It's a ten-minute walk.* |
| **You can't miss it.** | It's very easy to find. |
| **Got it.** | I understand. (informal) |

👂 Press play and follow the route on the map with your finger.

listen.text: Go out of the café, turn left and walk to the end of the street. The stop is opposite the big church. You can't miss it.
Get on at Hope Street and get off at Market Street. It's only three stops.
The phone shop is next to the bank. It's a two-minute walk from the stop.

parts.title: Quick checks on the map (not graded)

questions.q: The tram stop is ___ the church.

check.why: They face each other across the street → **opposite**.

questions.q: The phone shop is ___ the bank.

options: at the end of the street

check.why: Where Hope Street meets the other street → **on the corner**.

questions.q: You are on the tram. You arrive at your stop. You…

check.why: Leaving a tram/bus/train → **get off**. (Car or taxi → *get out of*.)

options: You must walk for ten minutes every day.

check.why: **a ten-minute walk** = the time it takes on foot (no -s on *minute* here!).
A friendly, fixed chunk after giving directions.

parts.title: Jess gives directions
parts.md:
Saturday morning. Nam asks Jess how to get to a phone shop. **Before you listen:** look at the map – can you guess the route?

**Listen in 3 rounds, at normal speed – don't stop, don't translate:**
1. **No transcript** – follow the story. 2. **With the transcript** – eyes on the words while you hear them. 3. **No transcript again** – notice how much more you hear.

listen.text: Morning, Jess! Can I ask you something? I need to buy a SIM card. Is there a phone shop near here?
There's one in the city centre, on Market Street. It's too far to walk, though. Take the tram.
The tram? OK. Where do I get on?
Go out of the café, turn left and walk to the end of the street. The stop is opposite the big church. You can't miss it.
Opposite the church. Got it. And where do I get off?
Get off at Market Street. It's only three stops, so it takes about ten minutes. The shop is next to a bank, I think.
Do I need to buy a ticket before I get on?
Yes, there's a machine at the stop. Or you can just tap your bank card. Unless you want to walk for an hour in the rain!
No, thanks. I've had enough rain this week. Thanks, Jess!

questions.q: What does Nam want to buy?
Why does Jess say *take the tram*?
How many stops, and how long does it take?
*"…**unless** you want to walk for an hour in the rain!"* – What does Jess mean?
options: If you don't want to walk an hour in the rain, take the tram.
You must walk for an hour.

questions.q: **Dictation:** type exactly what Jess says, starting with *"Go out of the café…"* (until *"street."*)
How much of this conversation did you understand on the **first** listen/read? Write a number, e.g. 75

parts.title: The fifteen-minute city
parts.md:
![A street for people, not cars](data/img/w1/l5-city.webp)

A short talk about an idea that is changing cities. Before you listen, think: **how many minutes from your home** are your work, a supermarket and a park?

**Listen in 3 rounds, at normal speed – don't stop, don't translate:**
1. **No transcript** – follow the story. 2. **With the transcript** – eyes on the words while you hear them. 3. **No transcript again** – notice how much more you hear.

listen.text:
Imagine you could get everything you need in fifteen minutes from your home – on foot or by bike. Your work, your school, the shops, a doctor, a park. This is the idea of the "fifteen-minute city".

The idea comes from Carlos Moreno, a professor in Paris. He noticed that many people spend hours every week in cars and on trains, just getting from one place to another. Rather than building bigger roads, he asked: why not bring daily life closer to people?

Paris made the idea famous. The city added hundreds of kilometres of bike lanes and turned some busy streets into spaces for people, not cars.

However, not everyone likes it. Some people worry that it will make it harder to drive. Others say it only works in big, rich cities.

In other words, the fifteen-minute city is a simple idea, but changing a real city is not simple at all. So, next time you walk to a shop, ask yourself: how many minutes does it take from your home?

options: A city where you can reach daily needs in 15 minutes on foot or by bike.
A city you can drive across in 15 minutes.
A city where shops open for only 15 minutes.

questions.q: Who had the idea, and where does he work?
*"**Rather than** building bigger roads, he asked…"* What did he NOT want?
What did Paris do? (one thing is enough)
Which word starts the part about people who **don't** like the idea?
How much of this talk did you understand on the **first** listen/read? Write a number, e.g. 75
